metadata.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles
metadata.abstract: We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact Kähler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations. Our proofs build on the purity theorem and descent lemma of Cattani, Kaplan, and Schmid. We extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles. We also establish formal analogs for projective bundle modules over Hodge--Lefschetz modules, with applications to tautological classes and descent on matroid Chow rings.

metadata.title: Braided Multisections and Akhmedov's Fake Quadrics
metadata.abstract: We give handlebody decompositions of the complements of the cyclic multisections in $\Sigma_g\times S^2$ constructed in~\cite{AB}. The 2-handle framings are induced by the product coordinates. We compute the integral homology of the complements from their handle chain complexes, including the torsion subgroup of $H_2$. For the degree pairs $(3,3)$ and $(2,4)$, we specify surface diffeomorphisms inducing the maps on first homology prescribed in~\cite{AY} and recover the integral first homology groups $(\Z/3)^2\oplus\Z/(3m)$ and $(\Z/2)^2\oplus\Z/(4m)$, respectively, for $m\geq1$. For the symmetric $m=1$ sum, we also give a simultaneous surface diagram of the relative product attachments and identify their product framings with the surface framings. The resulting symplectic sums are aspherical and symplectically minimal, and have the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$.

metadata.title: Coupled free energy and a diagonal approach to coupled Kähler-Einstein metrics
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the coupled free energy $F_{-\gamma}^{\rm cp}$ which is a natural generalization of the free energy functional defined by Berman. In the Fano case, our coupled free energy provides a diagonal approach to the coercivity of the coupled Ding functional. We also define the non-Archimedean coupled free energy $F_{-\gamma}^{\rm cp,NA}$ on the space of finite energy measures on the Berkovich analytification. As a consequence of the regularization process of the non-Archimedean entropy established by Boucksom-Jonsson, Chi Li and Trusiani, we prove that the existence of a unique coupled Kähler-Einstein metric is equivalent to the stability condition that there exists $\epsilon >0$ such that $F_{-1-\epsilon}^{\rm cp,NA} \geq 0$ on the space of measures associated with a test configuration for the anticanonical line bundle. As a coupled version of the work by Berman, we show that the law of the empirical measure satisfies a large deviation principle whose rate function is the coupled free energy under the assumption that a conjecture by Hultgren is true. We also introduce a coupled version of the microscopic stability thresholds and prove that a uniformly coupled Gibbs stable Fano manifold has a unique coupled Kähler-Einstein metric. This is a generalization of the results by Fujita-Odaka and Berman.

metadata.title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension five
metadata.abstract: We summarize a coordinate-free classification of five-dimensional real Lie algebras up to isomorphism. Rather than solving the overdetermined quadratic Jacobi system modulo $\mathrm{GL}(5,\mathbb{R})$, the method uses Levi--Malcev theory and nilradical stratification. In the non-solvable case, the Levi factor is three-dimensional, $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ or $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$, acting on a two-dimensional radical; this yields exactly five classes, including the indecomposable $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})\ltimes\mathbb{R}^2$. In the solvable case, Schur's bound on commutative subalgebras of $\mathfrak{gl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ implies $\dim\mathfrak{n}\in\{3,4,5\}$, eliminating one- and two-dimensional nilradicals. The nilpotent case $\dim\mathfrak{n}=5$ has nine classes: three decomposable and six indecomposable, including $\mathfrak{h}_5$ and two filiform algebras. For $\dim\mathfrak{n}=4$, classification reduces to normal forms of outer derivations for $\mathbb{R}^4$, $\mathfrak{h}_3\oplus\mathbb{R}$, and $\mathfrak{n}_4$ under automorphism and scaling. For $\dim\mathfrak{n}=3$, it uses two-dimensional abelian subalgebras of $\mathrm{OutDer}(\mathfrak{n})$ containing no nonzero nilpotent operators. The work also computes minimal faithful representation dimensions $\mu(\mathfrak{g})$, gives a dictionary with classical tables, and designs a deterministic identification algorithm.

metadata.title: On Submanifolds with constant Möbius Ricci curvature
metadata.abstract: In the Möbius geometry of submanifolds there exists an important Möbius invariant tensor called the Möbius metric which together with the Möbius second fundamental form, the Blaschke tensor and the Möbius form constitute a complete system of conformal invariants for umbilic-free submanifolds when the dimension $n \geq 3$. An umbilic-free immersion $f:M^{n}\to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ is said to have constant Möbius Ricci curvature if its Möbius metric has constant Ricci curvature. In this paper, we classify umbilic-free immersions $f:M^{n}\to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ with constant Möbius Ricci curvature, flat normal bundle and two distinct principal normal vector fields. We prove that a submanifold with constant Möbius Ricci curvature and flat normal bundle has closed Möbius form, and then we classify such submanifolds provided the Möbius form vanishes identically on $M^{n}$.

metadata.title: On a Dual Heterotic Kodaira-Spencer Theory
metadata.abstract: We consider a dual version of heterotic Kodaira-Spencer theory on a Calabi-Yau three-fold $X$ with background fluxes, related to the type I BCOV theory of Costello-Li. We implement the Green-Schwarz mechanism of Costello-Li, where the Beltrami differential plays the role of the Green-Schwarz field. On a compact Calabi-Yau three-fold with background gauge fluxes $F$, where $\mathrm{tr}(F^2)$ is trivial in cohomology, retaining gauge anomalies only and leaving gravitational anomalies to future work, we incorporate the Costello-Li Green-Schwarz mechanism into the classical deformation complex. This gives a theory governed by a nilpotent operator $\bar D$ on $Q=T^{1,0}X\oplus\operatorname{End}(V)\oplus T^{*1,0}X$, whose extension maps carry holomorphic derivatives, so that $(Q,\bar D)$ is not a holomorphic bundle. Using diagonal $\bar\partial^\dagger$-gauge, the one-loop gauge anomaly cancels, assuming that the extension maps of $\bar D$ do not modify it, which we argue is plausible. Introducing an auxiliary $(0,2)$-form, we construct a cubic interacting theory whose gauge symmetries are governed by an $L_3$ algebra. On compact Calabi-Yau three-folds, and for sufficiently small fields, we show that the equation of motion is equivalent to the Maurer-Cartan equation, together with a divergence-free constraint on the Beltrami differential. Finally we trivialise $\bar D$ locally to the Dolbeault operator. The (non-tensorial) transition maps glue into a quasi-holomorphic extension sheaf $\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}}$, for which we prove a Dolbeault theorem, $H^{0,q}_{\bar D}(Q)\cong\check H^q(\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}})$.

On a compact Calabi-Yau three-fold with background gauge fluxes $F$, where $\mathrm{tr}(F^2)$ is trivial in cohomology, retaining gauge anomalies only and leaving gravitational anomalies to future work, we incorporate the Costello-Li Green-Schwarz mechanism into the classical deformation complex. This gives a theory governed by a nilpotent operator $\bar D$ on $Q=T^{1,0}X\oplus\operatorname{End}(V)\oplus T^{*1,0}X$, whose extension maps carry holomorphic derivatives, so that $(Q,\bar D)$ is not a holomorphic bundle. Using diagonal $\bar\partial^\dagger$-gauge, the one-loop gauge anomaly cancels, assuming that the extension maps of $\bar D$ do not modify it, which we argue is plausible. Introducing an auxiliary $(0,2)$-form, we construct a cubic interacting theory whose gauge symmetries are governed by an $L_3$ algebra. On compact Calabi-Yau three-folds, and for sufficiently small fields, we show that the equation of motion is equivalent to the Maurer-Cartan equation, together with a divergence-free constraint on the Beltrami differential. Finally we trivialise $\bar D$ locally to the Dolbeault operator. The (non-tensorial) transition maps glue into a quasi-holomorphic extension sheaf $\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}}$, for which we prove a Dolbeault theorem, $H^{0,q}_{\bar D}(Q)\cong\check H^q(\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}})$.

metadata.title: Measures of maximal entropy for monotone factors of smooth surface diffeomorphisms
metadata.abstract: We prove that a transitive monotone factor of a smooth surface diffeomorphism has a unique measure of maximal entropy whenever its topological entropy is positive. Its entropy is the entropy of a single homoclinic class of the diffeomorphism, and the factor map is a measure-theoretic isomorphism on every ergodic measure with positive entropy of that class. The other homoclinic classes are mapped to periodic orbits. We give an application to the essential factor of a diffeomorphism isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov map ---possibly relative to a finite invariant set--- constructed by García-Sassi \& Tal: the essential factor has a unique measure of maximal entropy, which is Bernoulli and has full support.

metadata.title: Non-migration for planar elastic flows
metadata.abstract: We consider a closed planar curve evolving by the free or the length-preserving elastic flow. We prove that the scale-invariant bound $L\int k^2\,ds\le 4\pi^2+8/3$ at the initial time prevents the entire curve from crossing any line between two times. For the length-preserving flow, a quantitative gradient estimate controls the total centroid displacement.

metadata.title: Holomorphic sectional curvature and the Calabi operator on Kähler C-spaces
metadata.abstract: We study holomorphic sectional curvature and the Calabi curvature operator on compact Kähler manifolds. First we show that every homogeneous Kähler metric on a generalized flag manifold has positive holomorphic sectional curvature. For the standard homogeneous Kähler-Einstein metric with Einstein constant 2, it is shown that the spectrum of the Calabi operator lies in $(-2,2]$. We determine its sharp upper bound in terms of the anticanonical degrees and characterize the 2-eigenspace. The spectral bounds imply nonnegative cross quadratic bisectional curvature and positive dual cross quadratic bisectional curvature, proving conjectures of Ni and Zheng. We also show that these conditions do not characterize homogeneity: we construct a nonhomogeneous Kähler-Einstein 13-fold whose Calabi spectrum lies strictly inside $(-2,2)$ after the same normalization, as well as nonhomogeneous examples in dimensions 4 and 5. The proofs involve an integral identity for holomorphic sectional curvature, projective embeddings, root-space estimates, and explicit metrics on projective bundles.

metadata.title: Branched Covers and Fiberwise Degeneration along Weak Kähler Geodesics
metadata.abstract: On the projective line, we construct a pair of smooth Kähler potentials whose weak geodesic has isolated quadratic zeros of the fiber form at two fixed points throughout an interior time interval. The geodesic is smooth near these zeros, and its space-time form has constant rank one there. For the same fixed endpoints, the minimum fiber eigenvalue of the nondegenerate Monge-Ampère approximations tends to zero, answering AIMPL Problem 2.5 in the negative. The construction works on every compact connected Riemann surface with a prescribed Kähler form and realizes any positive even order of vanishing. Taking products yields higher-dimensional examples in which the fiber rank drops by one along a smooth hypersurface while the space-time form retains maximal rank nearby. The proof starts from a semipositive model built from a branched cover. We make its endpoints strictly positive by local corrections and use comparison along holomorphic curves to prove that the weak geodesic still agrees with the model on an explicit interior region. There a ramification point of local degree $m$ gives a fiber zero of order exactly $2m-2$.

metadata.title: Riemannian hypermaps to complex space forms
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we propose the notion of a \textit{hypermap}, defined as a Riemannian map whose range distribution is tangent to a real hypersurface of a complex space form. This construction leads to a new direction in Riemannian map theory. We establish the fundamental Gauss and Codazzi equations for a hypermap and use them to investigate the extrinsic geometry of its range leaves. In particular, when the ambient complex space form is non-Euclidean, we prove that these leaves cannot be totally umbilical and that their shape operator fails to be parallel. metadata.title: The residual map as a stratified fibration over the resonance arrangement
metadata.abstract: Given a stratum $\mathcal{H}(\mu)$ of meromorphic one-forms on a Riemann surface with prescribed orders of zeros and poles, the residual map assigns to each differential the collection of its residues at the poles. In this paper, we prove that the residual map is a locally trivial topological fibration over each open flat of the stratification induced by the resonance arrangement. To give an algebro-geometric proof of this result, we introduce a refined compactification of the projectivized stratum $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{H}(\mu)$, namely the moduli space of residue-aligned multi-scale differentials $\operatorname{RAMS}(\mu)$. We prove that the projectivized residual map extends to $\operatorname{RAMS}(\mu)$ as a stratified fibration over the projectivized resonance arrangement, thereby yielding a resolution of the projectivized residual map. This approach naturally extends to the analogue of the residual map for strata of $k$-differentials. Complementing the algebro-geometric approach, we also develop a flat-geometric point of view. In genus zero, each isoresidual fiber carries a canonical higher-dimensional analogue of a translation structure. These fibers admit a metric completion whose boundary has a modular interpretation in terms of the WYSIWYG compactification, for which we provide explicit local models. Isoresidual fibers admit a polyhedral cell decomposition whose geometry varies linearly with the underlying configuration of residues in period coordinates. Degenerations of these cells occur precisely when resonance conditions are satisfied, providing a geometric proof that the residual map is a stratified fibration. Finally, certain isoresidual fibers admit natural interpretations as Hurwitz spaces of branched covers, yielding unexpected homeomorphisms between moduli spaces of covers with prescribed ramification profiles.

metadata.title: Using Transformers to Generate 3-Manifold Triangulations
metadata.abstract: Using dehydration signatures as an encoding, we train GPT-2-style transformers to generate triangulations of 3-dimensional manifolds. Our main runs each use approximately 3 exaFLOPs, spanning a 200 million parameter model trained on 60 million sphere triangulations to an 11 million parameter model trained on 1.1 billion sphere triangulations. The optimal model has 10 blocks, width 640 and generates dehydration signatures of closed manifolds of various topological types at a rate of 6.9%, 82% of which are spheres. To investigate how our method scales, we use the technique of IsoFLOP curves on 15-tetrahedron triangulations of the 3-sphere, over a compute range of 6 to 3000 petaFLOPs, and observe neural scaling behaviour. We extract a parameter scaling exponent of $\alpha = 0.49$ ($[0.48, 0.50]$ stat, $\pm 0.02$ syst), and an optimal ratio of 234 tokens per parameter for training. In addition, we present a number of smaller experiments, including evidence that transformers are able to learn to count degree-one edges near-perfectly, but get progressively worse when counting edges with higher degrees.

metadata.title: The dimension-free threshold for maximal sections of $\ell_p$
metadata.abstract: We prove the existence of a sharp threshold $p_0 \approx 26.265\ldots$, such that for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\geq p_0$, the volume maximizing section of the unit ball of $\ell_p^n$ is the section with Ball's hyperplane $(\frac{e_1+e_2}{\sqrt{2}})^\perp$, whereas for $p\in(2,p_0)$ the asymptotic maximizer as the ambient dimension $n\to\infty$ is the hyperplane orthogonal to the diagonal vector $\frac{e_1+\cdots+e_n}{\sqrt{n}}$.

metadata.title: Rigidity and Classification of Manifolds with Maximal Boundary Static Kernels
metadata.abstract: Boundary static potentials arise from the adjoint equations associated with simultaneous variations of scalar curvature and boundary mean curvature. On a connected manifold of dimension $n\ge2$ with nonempty smooth boundary, the space of boundary static potentials has dimension at most $n$. We classify all complete manifolds attaining this bound. For $n\ge3$, every such manifold is isometric to a domain in a simply connected space form and has at most two boundary components. In dimension two, the classification also includes coverings of annuli and exteriors, as well as spherical Möbius bands. Finally, for $n\ge3$, the dimension hypothesis is sharp for constant-curvature rigidity, and for $n\ge2$, it is sharp for the bound on the number of boundary components.

metadata.title: Trans-Sasakian space forms
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we derive an explicit expression for the Riemann--Christoffel curvature tensor of a trans-Sasakian manifold with pointwise constant $\varphi$-sectional curvature and introduce the notion of trans-Sasakian space forms. As consequences, we obtain explicit formulas for the Ricci tensor and the scalar curvature. We further prove that every $3$-dimensional trans-Sasakian manifold necessarily has pointwise constant $\varphi$-sectional curvature. In addition, we investigate statistical structures on trans-Sasakian manifolds and introduce the notion of trans-Sasakian statistical space forms. We then establish a classification of such statistical structures. Our results show that every trans-Sasakian statistical space form of dimension greater than $3$ is necessarily almost-trivial. In the $3$-dimensional case, we establish a rigidity theorem for trans-Sasakian statistical space forms and provide explicit examples showing the existence of non-trivial $3$-dimensional trans-Sasakian statistical space forms

metadata.title: On the anisotropic mean curvature flow in the Gaussian space
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we study the anisotropic mean curvature flow in the Gaussian space endowed with a Finsler metric obtained from a Minkowski metric by a conformal deformation. We first derive the conformal transformation formulas for the fundamental tensor, the Cartan tensor, and the Chern connection of the conformally related Finsler metrics. Based on these formulas, we express the anisotropic mean curvature in the Gaussian space in terms of the corresponding anisotropic mean curvature with respect to the original Minkowski metric, and derive the associated evolution equation. Finally, we establish the short-time existence and uniqueness of smooth solutions by reformulating the geometric evolution equation as a strictly parabolic quasilinear partial differential equation.

metadata.title: Interlacing of the Volume and Half-Volume Spectra
metadata.abstract: We give a direct proof of the weak interlacing inequalities \[\omega_p\leq\widetilde{\omega}_p\leq\omega_{p+1}\] between the volume and half-volume spectra of a closed connected Riemannian manifold $M^{n+1}$, $n+1\geq3$. We also prove that, for a residual set of smooth metrics, the area of every smooth embedded half-volume CMC boundary lies outside the rational span of the areas of smooth closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces. For dimensions $3\le n+1\le 5$, these results yield strict interlacing for generic metrics and a lower bound of order $A^{n+1}$ for the number of distinct half-volume CMC boundaries with area at most $A$.

metadata.title: Construction of Transverse Metrics from Transversely Elliptic Operators on Foliated Manifolds
metadata.abstract: The existence of a transverse metric on a foliated manifold is typically used as a framework for studying transversely elliptic basic differential operators. metadata.title: Log-concavity and level set curvature estimates for the first Dirichlet eigenfunction in hyperbolic space
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we study the first Dirichlet eigenfunction on bounded, smooth and strictly horo-convex domains in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We prove its strict $\log$-concavity in arbitrary dimension and establish the Gauss curvature bound $K>1$ for its level sets. In dimensions two and three, we further obtain quantitative lower bounds for $K$ in terms of the minimum Gauss curvature of the boundary. In higher dimensions, the product of the two smallest principal curvatures of each level hypersurface exceeds one. Furthermore, we extend the strict $\log$-concavity result to bounded smooth horo-convex domains. Our approach combines maximum or minimum principles for suitable auxiliary functions, boundary convexity estimates and a domain deformation argument.

metadata.title: Generalized Hopf bifurcations: a homological analysis and obstructions to their existence
metadata.abstract: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation? Regarding (1), we compute the cohomology of the expelled attractors in terms of the cohomology of $K$; in the case of continuous-time dynamics this can be improved to a computation of their Borsuk shape. As for (2), we show that certain compacta cannot undergo generalized Hopf bifurcations and, when the ambient space has dimension $ \leq 3$, give a complete topological characterization of which can.

analysisBasis.abstract: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation? Regarding (1), we compute the cohomology of the expelled attractors in terms of the cohomology of $K$; in the case of continuous-time dynamics this can be improved to a computation of their Borsuk shape. As for (2), we show that certain compacta cannot undergo generalized Hopf bifurcations and, when the ambient space has dimension $ \leq 3$, give a complete topological characterization of which can.

metadata.title: Splay ostracism on ferroelectric nematic shells
metadata.abstract: Ostracism was the practice in use in Athens and other ancient Greek cities to send into exile citizens whose influence was deemed to be dangerous. Quite similarly, splay ostracism is here the approximation that bans splay distortion from thin films of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals on a curved shell in space. This reduces to a mere geometric problem the quest for equilibria of director vortexes and the walls isolating them, as splay ostracism requires the director field lines to be everywhere orthogonal to systems of geodesics on the shell. Consequences of this theorem are explored for shells with Gaussian curvature of either sign. The resulting quasi static dynamics reveals both cases where walls escape from the shell and cases where they are trapped on it, with possibly different reflections on the vortex dynamics.

metadata.title: On Grassmann $4$-designs
metadata.abstract: We prove that there is a unique tight $4$-design in the real Grassmannian $G_{2,4}$, up to the action of $O(4)$. Using symmetric association schemes, we also construct an $N$-point $4$-design in $G_{2,4}$ for every even integer $N\geq10$. metadata.title: Closed-form solution for semi-symmetric folding of waterbomb tessellations
metadata.abstract: Rigid-origami folding has versatile applications in the fields of architecture, engineering, medicine and aerospace. Given the design parameters of a single waterbomb cell, the global geometry of the origami tessellated shell at an intermediate state of folding is directly determined. Even though existing numerical methods of rigid-origami can be used to describe geometric forms, algebraic solutions of the waterbomb folding kinematics and tessellations reduce the algorithmic complexity and determine the range of admissible configurations exactly. The existing analytical solution for a symmetrically folded waterbomb cell and tessellation is extended to the case of a cell folded semi-symmetrically, i.e. a cell with a 180° rotation symmetry. The algebraic derivation provides the solution for the entire folding process. The resulting functional relationship between the design parameters and the 3D cell geometry of the folded waterbomb cell enables efficient studies of achievable shell geometries. This development facilitates a deeper understanding of the correspondence between the geometric parameters of a single waterbomb cell and the statically relevant geometric properties, i.e. the shell curvature and the effective cross-sectional height. The systematic description of this correspondence provides the basis for innovative design concepts using modern cementitious composites, e.g. textile-reinforced concrete, to produce thin-walled, high-performance, lightweight shells.

metadata.title: Biharmonic surfaces with flat normal bundle in the four-dimensional sphere
metadata.abstract: We prove that a proper biharmonic surface with flat normal bundle in the four-dimensional unit sphere $\mathbb S^4$ lies minimally in a small hypersphere of radius $1/\sqrt{2}$. Since the surfaces with constant mean curvature and those with parallel normalized mean curvature vector field are already understood, the core of the paper is the non-existence of biharmonic surfaces with flat normal bundle in $\mathbb S^4$ whose mean curvature is not constant and whose normalized mean curvature vector field is not parallel. We first show, adapting an argument of Fu, Hong and Yang, that the gradient of the mean curvature is a principal direction. Then the problem reduces to a first order system of ordinary differential equations with a constraint, and we show that this system has no admissible solutions by an elimination argument.

metadata.title: Diameter bounds for complexes that are close to flag or close to normal
metadata.abstract: The Hirsch problem asks how large the diameter of the dual graph of a simplicial complex can be, in terms of its number of vertices. For normal complexes, the classical bounds are the Larman-Barnette bound, which is linear for fixed dimension, the Kalai-Kleitman bound, which is quasi-polynomial, and the Adiprasito-Benedetti bound n-d, which however holds only for flag complexes. After sharpening the Larman-Barnette and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds, we study how the three bounds deteriorate when flagness or normality is weakened. We give three ways to quantify the distance from flagness, and in each case we bound the diameter in a way that interpolates between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Larman-Barnette bounds. We also quantify the distance from normality by a parameter q, and obtain a bound that is a polynomial of degree q in n. Finally, we conjecture a statement on flag layered families that would imply an interpolation between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds.

metadata.title: The first gap for minimal submanifolds in spheres
metadata.abstract: Let $f:M^n\to\Sn^{n+q}(1)$ be a minimal immersion of a closed connected manifold with $n\ge3$ and $q\ge2$, and let $S$ be the squared length of its second fundamental form. We prove an integral inequality that gives $\max_M S\ge n$ if the immersion is not totally geodesic. If $n\ne4$ or $q=2$, equality $\max_M S=n$ holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface; if $n=4$ and $q\ge3$, equality holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface or the standard minimal embedding of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ in $\Sn^7(1)$. Both classifications are understood up to an ambient isometry, a totally geodesic inclusion, and a finite covering. We construct the integral inequalities using polynomial weights and divergence identities. The required algebraic estimates are proved by sums of squared tensor norms.

metadata.title: Counting multigeodesics and the Selberg-Delange method
metadata.abstract: We study the counting function $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$ for $m$-multigeodesics of length at most $x$ on a compact hyperbolic surface $X$ where $m$ is a positive integer. Building on the Selberg-Delange method, originally developed for counting integers with exactly $m$ prime factors in the interval $[1,x]$, we prove a large $x$ asymptotic for $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$. We show that for fixed $m$ as $x\to\infty$ the asymptotic is independent of the surface, whereas for $\frac{m}{\log x}$ bounded away from zero, the asymptotic depends on an infinite Euler product over the lengths of primitive closed geodesics. We also study the distribution of the function $\omega_1$, defined on multigeodesics $\Gamma$ as $\omega_1(\Gamma)=k-1$ for $\Gamma=(\gamma_1,...,\gamma_k)$ a $k$-multigeodesic. We show that as $x\to\infty$, the distribution of $\omega_1$ in the set of multigeodesics of length $\leq x$ is close to that of a Poisson random variable with parameter $\log x$. Both of these theorems rely on studying the generating function of the random variable $\omega_1$ which we relate to the Selberg zeta function.

metadata.title: A diameter-one set in $\mathbb{R}^5$ that cannot be covered by six diameter-one balls
metadata.abstract: We construct a compact set of diameter $1$ in $\mathbb{R}^5$ which cannot be covered by six Euclidean balls of diameter $1$. Its convex hull is a full-dimensional convex body satisfying the same property. Moreover, a finite subset of diameter $1$ cannot be covered by six closed balls even when their radius is increased to $0.50001$. The compact set is the quadratic image of the unit sphere in the space of symmetric $3\times3$ matrices of trace zero. A hypothetical cover leads to twelve spherical ellipses covering ${\mathbb S}^2$ and arranged in six antipodal pairs. Using Euler's formula, we replace them by twelve pentagonal regions contained in the ellipses. An area estimate then gives a contradiction.

metadata.title: Classification of cohomogeneity one steady gradient Ricci solitons in dimension four and five
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we first prove Appleton's conjecuture on the uniqueness of noncollapsed steady solitons constructed in \cite{Appleton}. We also classify non-Ricci-flat $\kappa$-noncollapsed cohomogeneity one steady gradient Ricci solitons in dimension four and five. After passing to a finite cover, in dimension four, they must be the Bryant soliton or Appleton's noncollapsed 4d steady soliton; in dimension five, they must be the Bryant soliton or solitons constructed by Ivey--Dancer--Wang.

metadata.title: Shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces
metadata.abstract: We describe the shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces, through their global integrations and their homotopy Poisson algebras. We construct the adjoint symplectic groupoid of the surface explicitly, show that admissible curves integrate to embedded Lagrangian subgroupoids, which are 1-shifted Lagrangians, and characterize when their shifted intersections are clean. For a component of the degeneracy locus, a canonical Hamiltonian flow on its shifted self-intersection recovers the modular period. On the infinitesimal side, the homotopy Poisson algebra of a connected admissible curve not contained in the degeneracy locus is $L_\infty$-isomorphic to its underlying cochain complex, and its $L_\infty$-isomorphism class is determined by the total contact multiplicity. The brackets of arity at least two can be removed by a change of tubular neighbourhood exactly when all contacts are transverse. At tangential contacts, the binary bracket retains the modular vector field. We establish this distinction using a general characterization of the $L_\infty$-isomorphisms induced by changes of tubular neighbourhood, valid for arbitrary coisotropic submanifolds.

metadata.title: The index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators: I
metadata.abstract: This is the first of a series of papers which will be devoted to a study of the index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on closed Riemannian manifolds. The aim of the series is to discretise the index of the Dirac operator. On flat tori, this is achieved by the Wilson--Dirac operator of lattice gauge theory on a regular lattice. On a general closed Riemannian manifold, however, no regular lattice is available. As an intermediate step between the continuum Dirac operator and its discretisations, we introduce mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on any closed Riemannian manifold, defined by integrating covariant differences over distances comparable to a fixed length scale. In this paper, we define the index of the mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators via spectral flow and prove that it agrees with that of the continuum Dirac operator at all sufficiently small scales. The proof rests on an elliptic estimate uniform in the scale and a Rellich-type compactness theorem. In the second paper, we shall pass from mesoscopic operators to discrete Wilson--Dirac operators.

analysisBasis.abstract: This is the first of a series of papers which will be devoted to a study of the index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on closed Riemannian manifolds. The aim of the series is to discretise the index of the Dirac operator. On flat tori, this is achieved by the Wilson--Dirac operator of lattice gauge theory on a regular lattice. On a general closed Riemannian manifold, however, no regular lattice is available. As an intermediate step between the continuum Dirac operator and its discretisations, we introduce mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on any closed Riemannian manifold, defined by integrating covariant differences over distances comparable to a fixed length scale. In this paper, we define the index of the mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators via spectral flow and prove that it agrees with that of the continuum Dirac operator at all sufficiently small scales. The proof rests on an elliptic estimate uniform in the scale and a Rellich-type compactness theorem. In the second paper, we shall pass from mesoscopic operators to discrete Wilson--Dirac operators.

metadata.title: The isoperimetric problem in the Riemannian Heisenberg $3$-space
metadata.abstract: We prove that every closed weakly stable constant mean curvature surface immersed in the Riemannian Heisenberg space ${\rm Nil}_3$ is an embedded rotational sphere. As a consequence, we solve the isoperimetric problem in ${\rm Nil}_3$: the isoperimetric domains of ${\rm Nil}_3$ are exactly the regions enclosed by rotational constant mean curvature spheres, and for each prescribed volume there is a unique such domain, up to ambient isometry. For small volumes, the isoperimetric result was proved by Tomter in 1993.

metadata.title: Shades and Convexity of Hypersurfaces
metadata.abstract: Let $f\colon M^n\to\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq2$, be a smooth immersion of a closed oriented manifold, with Gauss map $\nu\colon M\to\mathbf{S}^n$. For each unit vector $u$, the shade $S_u\subset M$ is the set of points where $\nu$ makes an acute angle with $u$. We show that $f$ is a convex embedding if and only if every shade is contractible. More generally, if every shade is $k$-connected, then $f$ is a convex embedding provided that $n\leq 2k+1$, or $n=2k+2$ and $H_{k+1}(M;\mathbf{Z})=0$. On the other hand, for every $n\geq 2k+3$ there is a nonconvex embedding $f\colon\mathbf{S}^n\to\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$ all of whose shades are $k$-connected. These results give sharp answers to a question of H. Wente in all dimensions.

metadata.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
metadata.abstract: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.

metadata.title: Spheres with transitive families of CMC hypersurfaces
metadata.abstract: The goal of this paper is to investigate the following question: what geometric restrictions does the existence of a transitive family of constant mean curvature hyperspheres impose on a Riemannian metric on $\mathbb S^n$? The notion of a transitive family can be made precise through the theory of Zoll families developed by Ambrozio, Marques, and Neves. Within this framework, we partially extend their local rigidity theorem for even conformal factors on $\mathbb S^3$ to every dimension $n\ge4$, assuming each hypersphere in the minimal Zoll family has the area of a round equator. Moreover, we give a partial answer to the following higher-dimensional version of a question posed by Robert Bryant: must a metric on $\mathbb S^n$, conformal to the round metric and admitting a Zoll family of hyperspheres with a common nonzero constant mean curvature, have constant sectional curvature? Finally, we also investigate inverse problems in the spirit of Hangan, asking which metrics make a fixed family of geodesic spheres have a common prescribed mean curvature.

metadata.title: On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we prove that every complete noncompact two-sided properly embedded constant mean curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal. The result holds in every dimension. We assume no bounds on curvature or volume growth. This establishes the properly embedded case of the finite-index version of do Carmo's question. For nonzero mean curvature, we use the radii of inscribed balls to define a positive weight. This weight gives a polynomial bound on weighted volume, while its reciprocal satisfies a differential inequality involving the Jacobi operator. We combine these properties with stability outside a compact set to obtain finite total area. This leads to a contradiction.

metadata.title: Hyperpolarity of polar foliations of codimension two
metadata.abstract: We consider polar foliations of codimension two on compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces. In rank at least two, we prove that these foliations are hyperpolar, settling the remaining case of the hyperpolarity problem discussed by Lytchak. We show that, for irreducible spherical Coxeter quotients, the horizontal universal cover fails to be a spherical building precisely on the Cayley plane, where every such foliation is congruent to one of the two known homogeneous models.

analysis.progressType: 余维二polar叶状结构的hyperpolarity及Cayley例外刚性
analysis.workSummary: 定理A证明紧单连通不可约、rank≥2对称空间上的每个余维二polar奇异黎曼叶状结构均hyperpolar，即截面平坦，无齐性假设。关键定理C更允许环境可约，但要求各截面的常曲率为正且只有一个dual leaf，此时环境rank必为1。另一条结果在不可约球面Coxeter三角商的全局余维二范围内，识别horizontal universal cover不能成为球面building的环境恰为Cayley平面；其每个此类叶状结构均全等于SO(3)×G₂或SU(3)·SU(3)的轨道叶状结构，对应壁重数(1,5)、(2,3)。
techniques: 周期水平测地线与Jacobi算子的公共核分布
Ricci方程的非正平方恒等式
法指数映射恒等式及Wilking对偶叶流
Lytchak分解与水平度量的building覆盖
Cayley曲率的Clifford对合与小奇异叶刚性
analysis.breakthrough: 补上高rank不可约对称空间上一般polar叶状结构的余维二缺口；结合Lytchak高余维定理，除点叶状结构外均hyperpolar。Cayley分类无需预设齐性：由Δf₀=2m−104f₀得到小奇异叶第二基本形式约束，经Clifford符号矛盾证其全测地，再由距离及其Laplacian恢复一个完整正则叶和全局叶状结构。
analysis.limitations: 定理A保留紧、单连通、不可约、rank≥2及余维二；全文叶连通、截面完备，叶闭性援引polar几何结果，并非另行假设齐性。定理C的单一dual leaf条件不可删除（正文给N×S²反例）。building异常识别及两模型分类限全局叶状结构、不可约球面Coxeter商；第6节还明确正则叶正维，不能扩展到可约商或任意抽象局部building几何。horizontal拓扑不同于环境普通拓扑，Hopf群作离散deck群不能理解成普通基本群的紧Lie群结构。已读PDF第1–19页的定理/路线与关键论证，渲染第6、8、17、18页核对Ricci平方恒等式、法指数式、Clifford符号及距离Laplacian单调性；未独立逐行验证整篇及所引结果。外部依赖包括Lytchak分解与building结果、Wilking对偶叶流描述、Alexandrino–Gorodski basic函数限制定理、Alexandrino–Töben全局等焦性，以及Cayley全测地子流形和两齐性模型/其水平几何单连通性的既有分类。
